subject: Short-run restructure: credits vs minute-pool proposal
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@heliumai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-run restructure: credits vs minute-pool proposal

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together two concrete paths to keep your 30-day evaluation running smoothly without extending the calendar window: one based on a short top-up of credits, and another that restructures the minute-pool into a small committed bucket. I've attached a quick spreadsheet with the line items and price math (redwood-shortrun-options-v2.xlsx).

Quick summary: 
- Option 1 — Top-up credits: one-time credit top-up to cover peak P95 usage (14 days) at a 10% discounted rate. No change to contract, invoice as a one-off.
- Option 2 — Minute-pool restructure: convert remaining unconsumed minute-pool into a 30-day committed bucket with a 20% discount and prorated usage true-up at the end of the evaluation. Requires a short amendment/PO.

Which would you prefer us to surface to Procurement? If it helps, we can also do a hybrid: small credit top-up + smaller committed bucket.

Next steps: I can share a one-page amendment for Option 2 if you want Procurement to sign; Option 1 can be handled via email confirmation and an invoice.

Thanks —
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-shortrun-options-v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alex Torres <atorres@heliumai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run restructure: credits vs minute-pool proposal

Thanks, Priyom —

Appreciate the two options. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side: 
1) For Option 1 (credit top-up) — how granular are the credits (tokens vs minutes)? We run mixed workloads (batch embeddings + interactive chat) and worried about splitting the fungibility.
2) For Option 2 (minute-pool) — does the committed bucket lock us into a minimum once the eval ends, or is it purely a 30-day commitment that expires? Procurement typically dislikes rolling minimums.

Procurement asked whether a PO would be required for the amendment, and if Redwood can accept a PO net-30. I looped Procurement on this message (procurement@heliumai.com).

Best,
Alex
Director of ML, Helium AI
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@heliumai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run restructure: credits vs minute-pool proposal

Alex — thanks for the fast reply. Short answers first: credits are fungible across workloads (tokens and minute-accounting are reconciled at invoice time), and the committed bucket we propose for Option 2 is a fixed 30-day commitment that expires (no ongoing minimums after the window). 

More detail: 
- Option 1 (Credit top-up)
  - Mechanic: one-time purchase of X token-equivalent credits (we map usage to credits during invoicing).
  - Recommendation: cover P95 peak for next 14 days. Sample number in spreadsheet = 250k token-equivalent credits @ 10% off list.
  - Procurement: no contract amendment required; invoice with a reference note is sufficient.

- Option 2 (Minute-pool restructure)
  - Mechanic: convert the remaining minute-pool hours into a 30-day committed bucket priced at a 20% discount vs list. We add a one-page amendment that describes the window and automatic sunset.
  - Recommendation: best when you expect steady usage for the remaining evaluation window.
  - Procurement: we can accept PO net-30; amendment will reference the PO number for accounting.

Hybrid: small credit top-up (cover immediate spikes) + a smaller committed bucket to give predictable throughput during your remaining test. That reduces risk of a late spike causing throttling.

I've attached a draft PO template and the option spreadsheet. If Procurement is comfortable with net-30, Ben (cc'd) will spin up the amendment template.

Would you like me to produce a DocuSign-ready amendment for Option 2 today?

— Priyom
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run restructure: credits vs minute-pool proposal

Looping in legal/finance notes for clarity before we send anything live to Procurement at Helium: 
- We can accept a PO net-30 for the one-page amendment; finance needs PO number on invoice and amendment.
- Approvals: the 20% discount on Option 2 is within commercial discretion for AE + DC; anything deeper (>20%) needs SR (sales review).
- If we do a hybrid and they ask for an additional 5% as a customer-satisfaction concession, we'll need manager approval.

Priyom — if you think the concession might be necessary to close the PO today, confirm the ask and I'll escalate to Monica for quick approval.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations
From: Alex Torres <atorres@heliumai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@heliumai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-run restructure: credits vs minute-pool proposal

Thanks team — we reviewed both options internally. Procurement prefers Option 2 (minute-pool restructure) since it keeps billing predictable and aligns with our internal approvals. Net-30 PO is fine.

We have a PO template ready (attached) and are happy to sign the one-page amendment. Can you send the amendment and a DocuSign link? We need the amendment to reference the PO number (will provide PO# once DocuSigned).

If it's helpful, we're also open to a small credit top-up to cover the first 72 hours post-amendment; leave that optional in the amendment and we'll decide quickly.

Alex
Director of ML, Helium AI
